chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Muthanna from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a divorce that makes her not permissible to him until she marries another husband, so a slave married her, then divorced her, is the divorce demolished (nullified)?
He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.
Due to the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His Book: 'until she marries another husband'.
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is one of the husbands'.
ai.seo_question: Does a slave's marriage count as the 'other husband' required to make a wife permissible to her first husband after three divorces?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'taliq al-thalath' by confirming that a slave's marriage suffices to make the wife permissible to her first husband, based on the Quranic phrase 'until she marries another husband' (2:230). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the literal interpretation of 'zawj' (husband), indicating that the intermediate marriage need not be with a free man, thereby resolving scholarly debates on the conditions of 'naskh al-talaq'. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of the intermediate marriage for removing the permanent prohibition.
